newsitem.title: UK: U.K. price war may intensify after petrol tax.
newsitem.headline: U.K. price war may intensify after petrol tax.

text.p: A fierce price war among U.K. gasoline retailers may intensify after the government announced a three pence per liter increase on all petrol and diesel fuels, which was exactly what the oil industry expected.

European gasoline prices also may fall sharply because the tanks are full in the U.K., and supplies from the U.K., traditionally an exporter, will head either to the Continent or the U.S. for the next few weeks, they said.
"The excess gasoline in Europe has tended to go into secondary storage in the U.K. and now it is available for export," said Colin Birch, a consultant at Purvin and Gertz in London.
"There is not going to be any strength in Europe for the next month," he said.

Some U.K. retailers may try to grab market share from the bigger oil companies in the next few days by working off inventories built up before the budget and not pass the increase on to consumers right away, they said.
An intense price war among British retailers has already cut profit margins and resulted in the cheapest gasoline prices in Western Europe.

"Those who have stockpiled in anticipation of the budget have undergone some storage costs but they can now release that product and compete with product supporting the new higher rate of duty," said Peter Regnier, director of Oil Price Assessments Limited (OPAL).
He said that difference was about $60 a tonne.
"We could see a price war with a vengeance in the next three to four days if the oil companies see that the supermarkets don't pass on (the higher price) right away," he said.
European gasoline prices rose sharply ahead of the budget as the industry built up stocks to take advantage of the tax.
But prices are already about $30 below those highs and may have factored some of the post-budget blues.
"I think a lot of it was discounted," into prices, said a trader at a U.K. refinery.
The government had already committed itself to raising excise duty of gasoline by five percent annually plus the rate of inflation.
The tax, announced by Britain's Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke, takes effect from 1800 GMT on Tuesday.
Birch said NWE cargoes could fall about $20-$25 in December to average $200, delivered to a European port, from about $224 on Tuesday.
The U.K. produced 27.4 million tonnes of gasoline in 1995, with domestic demand eating only 22 million, he said.
U.K.'s pump prices for premium unleaded, 4-Star and diesel excluding taxes are the cheapest in Western Europe, and lowest including taxes except for Luxembourg and Spain, according to data from OPAL.
OPAL said 68 pct of all U.K. petrol sales are unleaded gasoline and that taxes prior to today accounted for 76 percent of the average 4-Star pump price.
